hint.text: Renaissance is the French word for rebirth. The Harlem Renaissance was seen as the rebirth of Black American art and was therefore labelled as a renaissance.

atoms.text: The Harlem Renaissance was an art movement in the 1920s in the Harlem neighbourhood in New York City. Harlem was a Black neighbourhood, and during this time it became a popular spot for dancing and other nightlife activities. This brought in extra money for the neighbourhood. For the first time, there were Black artists who were able to make a living by creating art.

There were famous Black artists before this, but there would only be one or two at a time. During the Harlem Renaissance, many Black artists became successful: there were poets, singers, musicians, painters and many more. Some people who became successful at this time were Langston Hughes, Zora Neale Hurston, Louis Armstrong, and Duke Ellington.

Through their art, many of these artists spoke about the unfair ways that Black Americans were treated. They also celebrated Black American culture, which had not been done before. Most popular culture before the Harlem Renaissance focused on white Americans. The Harlem Renaissance was a very exciting and important time in U.S. history. Many of these artists are still well-known and important today.
